newsitem.title: USA: U.S. PC shipments seen rising 13 percent in 1997.
newsitem.headline: U.S. PC shipments seen rising 13 percent in 1997.

text.p: Market research firm International Data Corp said in its initial forecast for 1997 on Wednesday that it expects the U.S. personal computer industry to ship 13 percent more units next year than in 1996.

IDC also said in a PC Market Outlook conference here that it now projects U.S. PC shipments for the current year will grow to 26.8 million units, up 16.6 percent over 1995, slightly below the 16.9 percent rate it had earlier predicted.

Eric Lewis, manager of personal systems research at IDC, said Intel Corp's announcement this week that its own revenues would rise at least five percent sequentially in the third quarter, above forecasts, supported IDC's projections.
"To me, it's confirmed we've been right all along, saying it's a pretty good year," Lewis said. "Last year, was a boom year. This isn't a boom year," he added.

Lewis noted the current growth rate is below last year's rate of around 23 percent. He forecast higher saturation levels in the big business market and less growth in the consumer market than initially anticipated.
He said in a presentation to industry officials that unit sales to the home market would grow 16.5 percent this year, but by compound annual rates of 12 percent over the next four years.

Likewise, medium and large businesses would grow by 17 percent this year, but a lower 9.6 percent annually compounded rate through the year 2000 as high penetration rates demonstrated increasing saturation of that market.

"We're running out of places to stick these PCs in larger businesses," he said. He forecast the small office market to grow briskly, around 12 percent a year through 2000, and slightly higher growth for education and the government.

"The U.S. is coming off a torrid growth period and is expected to post moderating growth rates through the year 2000," he said. "Unit shipments are projected to rise from 23 million in 1995 to 42.9 million in 2000."

IDC said its preliminary estimate for worldwide PC sales in 1996 anticipates 18.5 percent growth in unit shipments to 69.5 million, with growth tempering slightly in 1997 to 16.6 percent, or a total of 81 million units.
